caea65bb7f902811d98ae257c767274fee58b95a.summary: Kaspersky GReAT report, published 2017-02-08, on fileless attacks against enterprise networks, found during incident response at a bank. Attackers ran Metasploit Meterpreter in memory, used Windows SC and NETSH to install a service and set up tunnelling, and used Mimikatz to collect administrator passwords. Kaspersky found more than 100 enterprise networks infected with malicious PowerShell scripts in the registry, but could not confirm they shared one attacker. The report says attribution is almost impossible and names Carbanak and GCMAN only as the closest groups with similar techniques.

cab1d334efc14a7e9238a6349486de0763d4e0ab.summary: AhnLab ASEC reports that the Andariel group, which may cooperate with or be a subsidiary of Lazarus, targets South Korean organisations. It assumes Andariel is exploiting the Apache ActiveMQ flaw CVE-2023-46604 to install NukeSped and TigerRat backdoors, but has no direct logs confirming this. Related ActiveMQ attacks included HelloKitty ransomware, CobaltStrike and Meterpreter stager installs. The report advises patching and asset management.
